_what: Pinned versions and sha256 digests of the tools setup.sh installs to render this report and run its gates.
Taken from the snapy technical report's tools/env-pins.json (the same Quarto, TinyTeX and Universal Ctags
releases), which is where the digests were recorded; setup.sh refuses any download whose digest differs.

python.why: PYTHON_VERSION of .github/workflows/tech-report.yml is 3.12; 3.11 is what the derivation-check environments use

python_packages.why: the 'Install pyharp-report, Jupyter and pytest' step of .github/workflows/tech-report.yml, unchanged

quarto.why: QUARTO_VERSION of .github/workflows/tech-report.yml and the version README.md names

tinytex.why: the workflow asks quarto-actions/setup for tinytex: true; scheme 1 carries LuaLaTeX, and setup.sh adds the packages the book loads (KOMA scrreprt among them) with tlmgr from the pinned snapshot
_why_tlnet_repository: Pinning the TinyTeX tarball does NOT pin TeX: scheme 1 ships no koma-script at all, so the
class the book is built on is fetched at render time from whatever the default repository
serves that day. That is a rolling mirror, and it broke the report: koma-script 3.49.3
(2026/10/19) removed \ifstr, which book/_tex/theme.tex:30 calls, and the PDF died with
on a head written four days earlier against 3.49.2.
www.texlive.info keeps a dated, immutable tlnet snapshot per day, so naming one pins every
TeX package by date the way requirements.txt pins the Python ones. 2026/10/17 is the last
snapshot before koma-script 3.49.3 and gives 3.49.2 (2026/02/02), which has \ifstr.
setup.sh runs `tlmgr update --self` against this same snapshot first, because the tlmgr in
the TinyTeX tarball is older than the snapshot's and refuses to install until it matches.
That update is deterministic: the snapshot does not move.
\ifstr is deprecated in KOMA-Script and gone from 3.49.3. Pinning buys time, it does not fix
it; book/_tex/theme.tex should move to \Ifstr, which is its chapter owner's call.

universal-ctags.why: CTAGS_VERSION of the workflow and of tools/code_anchors.py
